title: Every hand-off between source code and your app is a place to tamper
captions: Code you depend on passes through several hands. You review the source, but you install a built package from a registry. Each arrow is a hand-off an attacker can use.
Source to build: the xz release tarballs held a line that was not in git. It ran a hidden script while the package was built.
Registry: PyTorch nightly used a package called torchtriton from its own index. Someone put a package with the same name on PyPI, and pip installed that one instead.
Build: a CI action is code too. In March 2025, attackers moved tags of tj-actions/changed-files to point to a malicious commit. Workflows that used the tag ran it.
Defenses, one per hand-off. A lockfile fixes the exact version and its hash. Provenance says which source and build made a package. A commit SHA cannot be moved like a tag.
